questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about NABARD?

I. NABARD was formed on the recommendation of Sivaraman Committee.

II. NABARD came into existence in 1980.

III. It was set up with an initial capital of Rs. 100 crore.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NABARD** was established on the recommendations of the **Sivaraman Committee** (Committee to Review Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development).
 
• **NABARD** came into existence on **12 July 1982**, not in 1980.
 
• It was set up with an initial capital of **Rs. 100 crore**, which was raised to Rs. 5000 crore fully subscribed by the Government of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **NABARD** stands for **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development**.

 
 
• It is an apex development financial institution in India.
 
• It is responsible for providing and regulating credit and other facilities to promote and develop agriculture, small-scale industries, cottage and village industries, handicrafts, and other rural crafts.
 
• NABARD also supports all other allied economic activities in rural areas, with a view to promoting integrated rural development and securing prosperity for rural areas.
 
• It is involved in policy planning and operations relating to agriculture and other economic activities in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Sivaraman Committee**
 
 
• The Committee to Review Arrangements for Institutional Credit for Agriculture and Rural Development, also known as the Sivaraman Committee, was set up by the Reserve Bank of India in 1979.
 
• The committee was chaired by B. Sivaraman.
 
• Its recommendations led to the establishment of NABARD to address the credit needs of the agricultural and rural sectors.

questions.question: The Indian Vice President is elected by an electoral college comprising members of _______________.

options.text: Rajya Sabha, Lok Sabha and State Legislative Council
Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Assembly

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**both the houses of Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vice President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament: the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.
 
• The election is conducted in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The Vice President serves a term of five years but can be re-elected.
 
• To be eligible for the position of Vice President, a candidate must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a member of the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electoral College**

 
 
• An electoral college is a body of electors chosen or appointed by a larger group, in this case, members of both houses of Parliament in India.
 
• The members of the electoral college vote to elect the Vice President of India.
 
 
 
• **Proportional Representation**
 
 
• Proportional representation is a voting system aimed at achieving a close match between the percentage of votes and the percentage of seats obtained by each party or group of candidates.
 
• This system ensures that minority groups have a chance of representation in the elected body.
 
 
 
• **Single Transferable Vote**
 
 
• The single transferable vote (STV) is a voting system designed to achieve proportional representation through ranked voting in multi-seat organizations or constituencies.
 
• Under STV, voters rank candidates in order of preference, and candidates are elected sequentially based on those preferences.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Vice President**
 
 
• The Vice President of India is the second-highest constitutional office in the country, after the President.
 
• The Vice President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• In the absence of the President, the Vice President assumes the duties and responsibilities of the President.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty?

options.text: To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote cooperative society**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Constitution of India specifies certain duties that every citizen is expected to perform, known as Fundamental Duties.

• These duties are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A.

• Promoting a cooperative society is not listed among the Fundamental Duties.

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Fundamental Duties**

• Fundamental Duties are moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.

• There are 11 Fundamental Duties listed in the Indian Constitution.

• These include duties such as respecting the National Flag and National Anthem, cherishing the noble ideals of freedom struggle, protecting the sovereignty and integrity of India, promoting harmony, and safeguarding public property.

• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**

• This amendment is also known as the Mini-Constitution due to the large number of changes it brought about in the Indian Constitution.

• It added ten Fundamental Duties to the Constitution under Article 51A.

• The act also made changes to various other parts of the Constitution, including the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, and Directive Principles of State Policy.

• **Swaran Singh Committee**

• The committee was set up in 1976 by the Indian government to make recommendations on Fundamental Duties and other constitutional amendments.

• It was chaired by Dr. Swaran Singh, who was a former Minister of External Affairs.

• The committee's recommendations led to the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution through the 42nd Amendment.

</ul

questions.question: How many officials are there for looking after each Kabaddi match?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• In Kabaddi, a typical match is overseen by **6 officials** who ensure that the game is conducted fairly and according to the rules.

• These officials include one referee, two umpires, a scorer, and two assistant scorers.

• The referee has the final authority on all decisions and is responsible for the overall conduct of the game.

• The umpires assist the referee and are responsible for judging points, fouls, and other infractions during the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Roles of Kabaddi Officials**

• **Referee:** The referee is the chief official of the game and has the ultimate authority in all decisions related to the game. The referee's role includes starting and stopping the game, ensuring the rules are followed, and making decisions on contentious issues.

• **Umpires:** There are two umpires in a Kabaddi match who assist the referee. They are responsible for observing the game and making decisions on points, fouls, and other infractions. The umpires work in coordination with the referee to ensure fair play.

• **Scorer:** The scorer is responsible for keeping track of the score, recording points, and maintaining the official score sheet. The scorer ensures that the score is accurately reflected on the scorecard.

• **Assistant Scorers:** There are two assistant scorers who help the main scorer in maintaining the score sheet. They also keep track of the timing, substitutions, and other administrative tasks during the match.

• **Kabaddi Game Overview:**

• Kabaddi is a contact team sport that originated in India. It is played between two teams of seven players each.

• The objective of the game is for a single player on offense, referred to as a "raider," to run into the opposing team's half, tag as many of their players as possible, and return to their own half without being tackled by the defenders.

• Points are scored for each player tagged, and the defending team earns points for stopping the raider.

• The game is played on a rectangular court, and each half lasts for 20 minutes with a 5-minute break in between.

• Kabaddi requires a combination of strength, strategy, and agility, making it an exciting and dynamic sport.

</ul

questions.question: In which town of India did James Prinsep conduct the census in 1824?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Allahabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• James Prinsep conducted the census in Allahabad in 1824.

• Allahabad is one of the prominent historical cities in India, known for its rich cultural and historical significance.

• James Prinsep was a British scholar, orientalist, and antiquary known for his work on Indian scripts and numismatics.

• The 1824 census conducted by Prinsep is one of the earliest recorded censuses in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **James Prinsep**

• James Prinsep was an English scholar, orientalist, and antiquary.

• He is best known for deciphering the Kharosthi and Brahmi scripts of ancient India.

• His work laid the foundation for the study of Indian epigraphy and numismatics.

• Prinsep served as the assay master of the mint of the East India Company in Benares (Varanasi).

• **Allahabad**

• Allahabad, officially known as Prayagraj, is a city in the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

• It is one of the oldest cities in India and holds significant historical and cultural importance.

• Allahabad is known for the Triveni Sangam, the confluence of three rivers: the Ganges, the Yamuna, and the mythical Sarasvati.

• The city is also famous for hosting the Kumbh Mela, one of the largest religious gatherings in the world.

• **Census in India**

• The first comprehensive census of India was conducted in 1871 by the British administration.

• The census is a crucial exercise for collecting demographic data and is conducted every ten years.

• The Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India oversees the census operations.

• The data collected through the census is used for policy making, planning, and administration at various levels of government.

</ul

questions.question: Where is the National Flag hoisted by the Prime Minister on every Independence Day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Red Fort, located in Delhi, is a historic fort which served as the main residence of the Mughal Emperors.
 
• Every year, on 15th August, the Prime Minister of India hoists the national flag at the Red Fort to mark the celebration of Independence Day.
 
• The tradition of hoisting the national flag at the Red Fort started on the first Independence Day in 1947 when Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru hoisted the flag.
 
• The Red Fort is a symbol of India’s rich history and cultural heritage and is also a UNESCO World Heritage site.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Independence Day in India**

 
 
• Independence Day is celebrated annually on 15th August to commemorate India’s independence from British rule in 1947.
 
• The day is marked by flag hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural events, and the Prime Minister’s speech at the Red Fort.
 
• It is a national holiday in India, and the celebrations are also held in schools, colleges, and various institutions across the country.
 
 
 
• **Red Fort**
 
 
• The Red Fort (Lal Qila) was constructed by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the mid-17th century (1638-1648).
 
• The fort is known for its massive enclosing walls of red sandstone and serves as an architectural masterpiece representing Mughal architecture.
 
• It houses several museums and historical structures, including the Diwan-i-Aam (Hall of Public Audience) and Diwan-i-Khas (Hall of Private Audience).
 
• The Red Fort is also a symbol of India’s struggle for freedom and holds immense historical significance.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister’s Speech**
 
 
• On Independence Day, the Prime Minister delivers a speech from the ramparts of the Red Fort, addressing the nation.
 
• The speech includes reflections on the nation's achievements in the past year, goals for the future, and tributes to freedom fighters and national heroes.
 
• This tradition was started by India’s first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, in 1947.

questions.question: Which of the following states is associated with the devotional folk dance ‘Gambhira’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Gambhira** is a devotional folk dance performed in the region of Malda in **West Bengal**.

• This dance form is associated with the worship of Lord Shiva, and it typically involves intense and devotional performances.

• Gambhira dance is usually performed during the festival of Chaitra Sankranti, marking the end of the Bengali year.

• The performers wear traditional attire and use masks to represent various deities and characters from Hindu mythology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Devotional Folk Dance:**

• Devotional folk dances are traditional dance forms that are performed as an expression of devotion and reverence towards deities.

• These dances are often integral parts of religious ceremonies and festivals in various regions of India.

• They combine music, dance, and drama to narrate stories from mythology and religious texts.

• Examples of devotional folk dances include Bhakti Dance, Kirtan, and Rasa Lila.

• **Gambhira Festival:**

• The Gambhira festival is a significant cultural event in the Malda district of West Bengal.

• It is celebrated with great fervor and enthusiasm, featuring performances of the Gambhira dance.

• The festival showcases the rich heritage and traditions of the region, attracting both locals and tourists.

• **Traditional Attire and Masks:**

• Performers of Gambhira dance wear traditional costumes that include vibrant and colorful attire.

• Masks are an essential part of the dance, representing various deities, animals, and mythological characters.

• The use of masks adds a dramatic element to the performance, making it visually captivating.

• **Chaitra Sankranti:**

• Chaitra Sankranti marks the last day of the Bengali calendar year and is celebrated with various cultural and religious activities.

• It is a time for reflection, thanksgiving, and preparation for the new year.

• Festivities include traditional dances, music, and rituals to honor the gods and seek blessings for the upcoming year.

</ul

questions.question: Murad Ali is a well-known _________ player.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Murad Ali is recognized as an accomplished player of the **sarangi**, a traditional Indian string instrument.

• The sarangi is known for its deep, resonant sound, which closely resembles the human voice.

• Murad Ali has contributed significantly to the preservation and popularization of sarangi music both in India and internationally.

• He comes from a family with a rich musical heritage, and he has been trained by some of the most respected musicians in the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Sarangi**

• The sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument from the Indian subcontinent, used in Hindustani classical music.

• It is known for its rich and warm sound, which has the ability to closely mimic the human voice, making it an ideal accompaniment for vocal performances.

• The sarangi is traditionally made from a single block of tun (red cedar) wood and has three main playing strings, usually made of gut, and around 35 sympathetic strings.

• It is played with a bow, and the musician uses the cuticles of the fingers to press the strings, which requires great skill and dexterity.

• **Guitar**

• The guitar is a popular string instrument that is played by plucking or strumming its strings, which are typically made of nylon or steel.

• It comes in various forms, including acoustic, electric, and classical guitars, each suited to different genres and playing styles.

• The guitar has a long history and is used extensively in many types of music worldwide, from classical to rock, jazz, and folk.

• **Tabla**

• The tabla is a percussion instrument consisting of a pair of hand drums, used in traditional Indian music.

• It consists of two drums, the smaller dayan and the larger bayan, each producing different sounds and pitches.

• The tabla is known for its complex rhythmic patterns and is an essential component of Hindustani classical music.

• **Flute**

• The flute is a wind instrument made from metal or wood, played by blowing air across an opening to create sound.

• It is used in various musical genres, from classical and jazz to folk and contemporary music.

• In Indian classical music, the bamboo flute (bansuri) is a popular instrument, known for its smooth, melodious tone.

</ul

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian to conduct a major British orchestra in 1961? He was the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra's 'Music Director for Life'.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zubin Mehta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Zubin Mehta was the first Indian to conduct a major British orchestra in 1961.

• He was born in Mumbai, India, and is known for his contributions to Western classical music.

• He has served as the Music Director for Life of the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra.

• Mehta has conducted the Vienna Philharmonic, the Berlin Philharmonic, and the New York Philharmonic, among other prestigious orchestras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Zubin Mehta**

• Zubin Mehta was born on April 29, 1936, in Mumbai (then Bombay), India.

• He studied music in Vienna, Austria, and quickly rose to prominence as a conductor.

• Mehta became the Music Director of the Montreal Symphony Orchestra in 1961, and shortly thereafter, he began his long association with the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra.

• In addition to his work with the Israel Philharmonic, Mehta has held positions with the Los Angeles Philharmonic and the New York Philharmonic, among others.

• **Israel Philharmonic Orchestra**

• The Israel Philharmonic Orchestra (IPO) is one of Israel's leading cultural institutions and is recognized worldwide for its artistic excellence.

• It was founded in 1936 as the Palestine Orchestra by Polish violinist Bronisław Huberman.

• The IPO has played a major role in the cultural life of Israel, performing throughout the country and on international tours.

• Zubin Mehta was appointed as the Music Director for Life of the IPO in 1981, a position he holds to this day.

• **Western Classical Music**

• Western classical music refers to a tradition of music that has its roots in the liturgical and secular music of the Western world, spanning from the medieval period to the present.

• This genre of music includes various forms such as symphonies, operas, chamber music, and choral works.

• Notable composers in Western classical music include Ludwig van Beethoven, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, Johann Sebastian Bach, and many others.

• Western classical music is characterized by its use of sophisticated harmonic structures, orchestration, and formal design.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an independent constitutional body according to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **NITI Aayog** stands for the National Institution for Transforming India.

• It is a policy think tank of the Government of India, established with the aim to achieve sustainable development goals and to enhance cooperative federalism by fostering the involvement of State Governments in the economic policy-making process.

• NITI Aayog was formed on **1 January 2015**, replacing the Planning Commission of India.

• Unlike the Planning Commission, it is not a constitutional body but operates as an executive body and advisory in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)**

• It is a constitutional body under Article 315 of the Indian Constitution.

• UPSC is responsible for conducting examinations for appointment to the services of the Union.

• It is an independent body to ensure impartial recruitment for the civil services and posts.

• **Election Commission of India**

• The Election Commission is a constitutional body under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution.

• It is responsible for administering election processes in India at national and state levels.

• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies.

• **State Public Service Commission**

• State Public Service Commissions are constitutional bodies under Articles 315 to 323 of the Indian Constitution.

• They conduct examinations for recruitment to state services and advise the government on various service matters like promotions and transfers.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution is related with organisation of village panchayats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Article 40 of the Indian Constitution directs the State to organize village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.

• This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) which are non-justiciable in nature but act as guiding principles for the state in governance.

• The inclusion of Article 40 highlights the emphasis placed by the framers of the Constitution on decentralized governance and grassroots democracy.

• Village Panchayats, as envisioned under Article 40, play a crucial role in rural development and local self-governance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

• The Directive Principles of State Policy, enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.

• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.

• **Village Panchayats**

• Village Panchayats are local government bodies at the village level in India.

• They are responsible for the administration of local affairs and implementation of various government schemes and policies related to agriculture, health, education, sanitation, and public works.

• Through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992, Panchayati Raj Institutions were given constitutional status, thereby strengthening local self-government.

• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**

• This amendment provided a constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions, ensuring a three-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all States having a population of over 2 million.

• It introduced provisions for the regular, free, and fair elections to these bodies.

• It also provided for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and women in Panchayats, ensuring inclusivity in local governance.

</ul

questions.question: The ‘Shiksha Karmi’ initiative and the ‘Lok Jumbish’ programme are schemes that helped increase the literacy rate of which state in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The 'Shiksha Karmi' initiative was launched in Rajasthan to improve the quality of education and enhance the literacy rate in the state.

• The 'Lok Jumbish' programme, initiated in 1992, aimed at promoting community-based education and making primary education accessible to all children in Rajasthan.

• Both these initiatives focused on innovative teaching methods, community involvement, and improving infrastructure in rural schools to boost literacy rates.

• These schemes have been instrumental in bridging the gender gap in education and increasing enrollment rates in schools in Rajasthan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Shiksha Karmi Project (SKP)**

• The Shiksha Karmi Project was launched in 1987 in Rajasthan by the Government of India in collaboration with Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA).

• Its main goal was to address teacher absenteeism and improve the quality of education in remote and rural areas by employing local educated youth as 'Shiksha Karmis' (education workers).

• The project focused on regular training, community involvement, and the use of innovative teaching methods to improve learning outcomes.

• The Shiksha Karmi Project received significant recognition for its impact on rural education and was considered a model for other states.

• **Lok Jumbish Programme**

• Lok Jumbish, meaning 'People’s Movement', was launched in 1992 in Rajasthan to create a decentralized and participatory approach to primary education.

• The programme emphasized the active participation of local communities, NGOs, and government bodies in planning and managing educational activities.

• It included various components such as school mapping, micro-planning, and the development of innovative teaching-learning materials.

• Lok Jumbish aimed to ensure universal primary education, particularly focusing on girls and marginalized sections of the society.

questions.question: The main objective of which of the following schemes is to support sustainable production in the agriculture sector by providing financial assistance to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of unforeseen events?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) was launched by the Government of India in 2016 to support sustainable agriculture production by providing financial assistance to farmers.

• Its primary objective is to provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases.

• The scheme aims to stabilize the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming, thereby promoting food security, crop diversification, and enhancing growth and competitiveness of the agriculture sector.

• Under this scheme, farmers pay a very nominal premium, and the government bears the remaining financial burden.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)**

• It is a scheme that promotes organic farming methods and aims to improve soil health and organic content of the soil.

• It encourages farmers to use traditional methods of farming and reduce dependence on chemical fertilizers and pesticides.

• The scheme also aims to increase domestic production and consumption of organic produce.

• **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)**

• Launched in 2015, this scheme aims to improve on-farm water use efficiency through micro-irrigation and ensure access to irrigation to every farm ("Har Khet Ko Pani").

• PMKSY focuses on creating new water sources, repairing and restoring traditional water bodies, and promoting efficient water use technologies.

• **Gramin Bhandaran Yojana**

• This scheme aims to create scientific storage capacity for storing farm produce, processed farm produce, and agricultural inputs.

• It helps in reducing post-harvest storage losses and provides farmers with better storage facilities to store their produce until they get remunerative prices.

</ul

questions.question: Who described Archimedes' method of finding the specific gravity of substances using a balance in the treatise ‘The Little Balance’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galileo Galilei**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer, physicist, and engineer, sometimes described as a polymath from Pisa.

• He is known for his contributions to modern physics and observational astronomy.

• In his treatise 'The Little Balance' (La Bilancetta), Galileo described Archimedes' method of determining specific gravity using a balance.

• This work was one of Galileo's earliest scientific writings, and it showcases his understanding of Archimedean principles and their practical applications.

• They played a significant role in the local administration and governance.

• A Kotwal was the chief police officer of a city, responsible for maintaining public order and safety.

questions.question: Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao Yojana is a campaign under the Government of India that was established for generating awareness and improving the efficiency of the welfare services intended for ________ in India.

• The "Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao" campaign was launched by the Government of India to address the declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues of women's empowerment over a life-cycle continuum.
 
• This initiative aims to prevent gender-biased sex-selective elimination, ensure the survival and protection of the girl child, and ensure education and participation of the girl child.
 
• Launched on 22nd January 2015, the campaign aims to create awareness and improve the efficiency of welfare services meant for girls in India.
 
• The initiative is a joint effort of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Ministry of Human Resource Development.

• It was launched with a specific focus on districts with low Child Sex Ratio (CSR).
 
• The BBBP scheme also involves the participation of various stakeholders including government officials, NGOs, and the public to promote the cause of the girl child.
 
• It is a comprehensive program that includes advocacy, community mobilization, and multi-sectoral interventions to ensure the rights of girls.
 
• It aims not only to address the problem of gender-based discrimination but also to promote the rights and welfare of girls in India.
 
 
 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):**
 
 
• CSR is defined as the number of girls per 1000 boys in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• The declining CSR is a significant concern as it reflects the deep-rooted societal preference for sons over daughters.
 
• The BBBP scheme aims to address the causes and consequences of the declining CSR and promote the value of the girl child.

• It includes the concept of equal rights and opportunities for women and men, girls and boys.
 
• Efforts like the BBBP scheme aim to promote gender equality and eliminate gender biases and discrimination.

questions.question: The Five Kingdom Classification of living organism was first proposed by:

__

• RH Whittaker was an American ecologist who was the first to propose the Five Kingdom Classification in 1969.

• The Five Kingdom Classification system includes Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

• Whittaker's classification was based on distinct characteristics such as cellular organization and modes of nutrition.

• This system helped to simplify the classification of living organisms and is widely accepted in the field of biology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Charles Darwin**

• Charles Darwin is best known for his contributions to the science of evolution.

• He proposed the theory of natural selection in his book "On the Origin of Species" published in 1859.

• While he made significant contributions to biology, he did not propose the Five Kingdom Classification system.

• **Aristotle**

• Aristotle was an ancient Greek philosopher and scientist who made early attempts to classify living organisms.

• He classified organisms into two groups: plants and animals.

• His classification was based on simple morphological characteristics and is considered outdated compared to modern systems.

• **Five Kingdom Classification**

• The Five Kingdom Classification system was proposed by RH Whittaker in 1969.

• The five kingdoms are Monera (Prokaryotes), Protista (single-celled eukaryotes), Fungi, Plantae, and Animalia.

• This system considers factors such as cell structure, mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

• It helps in understanding the diversity of life forms and their evolutionary relationships.

questions.question: Humayun Tomb, which is located in _________ is an example of Mughal architecture inspired by Persian architecture.

• **Humayun's Tomb** is located in **Delhi** and is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture.
 
• It was commissioned by Humayun's first wife, **Empress Bega Begum**, in 1569-70.
 
• The tomb was designed by the Persian architect **Mirak Mirza Ghiyas**.
 
• This monument was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent and is a UNESCO **World Heritage Site**.

• Mughal architecture is a distinctive Indo-Islamic architectural style that developed in the Indian subcontinent from the 16th to the 18th centuries.
 
• It is characterized by large bulbous domes, slender minarets with cupolas at the four corners, large halls, massive vaulted gateways, and delicate ornamentation.
 
 
 
• **Persian Architecture**
 
 
• Persian architecture is known for its intricate brickwork, tilework, and stucco decoration.
 
• It has influenced a variety of architectural styles in the Islamic world.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site**
 
 
• A UNESCO World Heritage Site is a landmark or area with legal protection by an international convention administered by the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).
 
• Such sites are designated for having cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance.
